FOUR! Whips it away! Ali tosses it up on the stumps, Marsh comes dancing down the track, takes it on the full and whips it cleanly through the gap at mid-wicket for a boundary. Good positive intent from Shaun Marsh.
A bit flatter and served on off, Shaun stonewalls it.
Floated ball around middle and off, blocked off the front foot and into the ground.
Skips down the track to a flighted ball and eases the drive to short cover.
Starts off with a loosener! Short and spinning away outside off, Marsh camps back and cuts it behind point to collect a couple.
Welcome back for the second session. England will have their tails up for sure. Can the spinners weave their magic? Remains to be seen. Moeen Ali to bowl. Shaun Marsh to face. Let's play...
... Day 3, Session 2 ...

Right then! The spinners have come to the party. They have got enough purchase off the deck and it would be interesting to see how the Aussie batsmen respond. Shaun Marsh has just arrived. He is known to be a good player of spin and has a set Khawaja for company. The deficit is down to 69. Can England turn things around or will the hosts prevail again? Don't go anywhere, we'll be back in a short while.

Drama towards the end has just spiced the session up! Phew! Crane would be cursing himself as he could have got rid of another set batsman, Usman Khawaja, in the last over before lunch had he not overstepped. The session began with the overnight batsmen making merry on the flattened-out wicket and thereby keeping the scoreboard moving. Both Khawaja and Smith registered their personal milestones and it seemed like these two will dominate the proceedings but Moeen Ali had other ideas. He was brought back into the attack before lunch and struck immediately to send the big fish, Smith, packing to calm some nerves in the English camp.
That must have stung! Short ball outside off, Khawaja rocks back and pulls it with the spin. It hits Stomeman at short leg who is down in pain. Nothing serious though and that's LUNCH ON DAY 3!
Leans forward and buries it into the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Crane has OVERSTEPPED! Mason, what have you done, son? A spinner doing this is a sin! England can't believe it and understandably so. It's pitched outside off, turning back in, Khawaja leans across and doesn't offer any stroke. In fact, he was hiding his bat behind his front leg. The ball hits the front pad and lobs to short leg. They all appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Root, Bairstow and Crane come together and the English skipper takes the review. It's seen that Crane has nothing behind the line and that is it. The story doesn't end here. If you are an England fan don't read this - Hawk Eye shows the impact is outside the line but it would have hit the stumps. Since no shot was offered, the on-field call would have been reversed. Reprieve for Usman, disappointment for England, although the review is retained. What's with the debutants this series? Tom Curran overstepped at the MCG in what could have been his maiden Test wicket then and now Crane joins him by doing the same.
It's all happening out there. Mason Crane convinces his skipper to take the DRS against Khawaja. Have England got another?
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

In the air... just short of Crane! He floats it up outside off, Usman Khawaja comes down the track to defend but the ball spins back in, hits the pad first and then the bat. The ball lobs back towards the bowler as Crane comes sprinting in to his right and dives in an attempt to take it with his right hand but the ball lands just short.
Spins back in, Marsh works it off the inner half through square leg for a single.
Comes down the track and whips it through mid-wicket does Marsh to get off the mark. Excellent over from Moeen Ali. He strikes immediately.
Gets nicely forward and blocks it into the ground.
Beaten! Ali lands it around middle, Marsh comes forward to defend but the ball turns away and beats the outside edge of Marsh's bat.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Very full on middle and off, jammed out towards mid off.
Shaun Marsh is the new man in. A bat pad and slip for him.

OUT! Caught and bowled! Ladies and gentlemen, England have got rid of Steven Smith! He misses out on a ton at his home ground and is fuming as he walks back. Boy, Moeen Ali is amongst the wickets, finally! Stop the press! Ali from around the wicket bowls a loopy delivery on middle and leg, Smith comes down the track to drive it against the spin but ends up getting it off the inner half back to the bowler. Ali crouches really low to pluck it just inches above the ground. He takes and claims it immediately. The umpire agrees and the Aussie skipper departs. Totally against the run of play. The 188-run stand comes to an end.
Moeen Ali is brought back into the attack.

That stayed a bit low! Loopy delivery, pitched on the rough outside off. Khawaja gets down to sweep but the ball spins back in, stays low and sneaks under his bat and then goes into the keeper's gloves.
Loopy ball outside off, SS presses forward to drive it through cover for a single.
Almost a replica of the previous ball.
On a flatter trajectory, Steven has got nothing to do with that one.
Floats it up around middle and leg, Smith leans forward in defense.
Leg spinner around middle, turning towards off, Smith hangs back to punch it back to Mason.
On middle and leg, nudged towards the leg side.
Good length delivery outside off, pushed towards the cover region.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Short of a length delivery, kicking a bit off the deck, Khawaja takes his bottom hand off to keep it out.

FOUR! Finesse! Curran comes from around the wicket and angles it in on the pads, Khawaja comes across a touch and flicks it neatly through mid-wicket. Made amazing connection as the ball races away to the fence.
Pounds in a short ball on middle, pulled with ease through mid-wicket for a single.
Works it with the spin past short leg for nothing.
Lovely shot! Crane gives it nice flight again, it's full outside off, Smith makes room and drives it through extra cover. Malan gives it a chase and slides to save a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Another feat for Steven Smith! He now becomes the Aussie captain with second most runs (682) in an Ashes series, only behind Sir Don Bradman! Incredible stuff. Flighted ball, landed outside off, eased through cover for a couple.
Loops it around off, defended down into the ground.
Tossed up delivery on middle and off, blocked off the front foot.
Mason Crane to roll his arm over.
Fullish outside off, Khawaja eases it through mid off. Broad gives it a chase to keep them down to two.
Gets forward and pats it nicely towards the cover region.
Fuller on the stumps, driven towards mid on.

Back of a length delivery outside off, Smith could have punched it through the line but he knows there is a big gap at mid-wicket and hence whips it off the inner half wide of Broad at mid on and takes three.
Fuller and angling in on off, Smith brings his bat down at the angle but gets it off the outer towards cover.
Starts off from over the wicket and lands it in the corridor of uncertainty, Smith yawns at it.
Tom Curran is back on.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Stays back and keeps it out. Anderson is bowling tidy lines but without any success.
Back of a length and rising a bit off the deck, Khawaja hangs back to defend but gets it off the splice. The ball dies down safely in the cover region.
Fuller in length and angling in from outside off, Usman stays rock solid in defense.
Outside off, Khawaja ignores.
Good length delivery on off, defended back to the bowler.

What was that? Too funny I tell you! Broad bangs in a short one, Smith initially tries to duck but then realizes that the ball isn't too short to do so. So what does he do now? He keeps his eyes on the ball, crouches low and swat-pulls it somehow back to the bowler. Seemed funny and even the skipper was seen having a laugh with his partner.
Fuller and angling in at the base of the stumps, Steven Smith stays leg side to jam it out towards the left of the bowler.
Sprays it a bit wider outside off, left alone without much fuss.
Clips this length ball on middle and leg through square leg for one.

FOUR! Controlled, along the ground, says Clarke on air! Broad once again bowls it short but without much venom behind it. It comes up at a good height as Khawaja stays rooted inside the crease and with a minimal swivel he pulls it really well to send it across the mid-wicket fence. Gets appreciation from Smith too.
Shortish delivery on middle and off, Smith looks to pull but mistimes it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Good length delivery on middle and off, Usman defends with a straight blade.

Good stop, Root! Anderson keeps probing in that zone outside off, it comes in first and then shapes away after hitting the deck. Khawaja gets squared up a touch as he tries to poke at it. He does so with soft hands and hence gets an edge which goes on the bounce to slip cordon where Root makes a diving one-handed stop to his left. Saved some runs for his side.
Anderson bowls a cutter outside off, Usman points his bat skywards and makes a leave.
Very full outside off, Khawaja nicely pats it towards the cover fielder.
Gets forward and across and gently defends it towards the off side.
Harmless ball in the sixth stump channel, not going after it says Uzzie lad.
Stuart with a short one but not that threatening. Khawaja gets on top of it as he eases the pull through square leg to keep strike.
Marginally fuller, angling across the southpaw, defended down.

FOUR! That's as good as anything! Broad overcooks it, serves it just outside off. Khawaja presses forward and caresses it off the meat. Pierces the gap at extra cover and picks up another boundary to his name.
Tries to ease it down the ground and does so but the mid off fielder is quick to get to his left and make a stop.
Short of a length delivery, angling in on middle and leg, Smith gets inside the line and rolls his wrists over the pull and sends it towards backward square leg for a single.
Fuller in length and angling in, Smith leans forward a touch and pushes it straight towards mid off.
Fuller and angling in, defended down watchfully.
Good delivery! Comes in from around off, Khawaja looks to defend but then zips away to beat the outside edge by a whisker.
Back of a length outside off, blocked down.
Played with soft hands! Good length delivery once again hurled outside off, Khawaja prods across and with soft hands tries to dab it away but gets a soft edge which rolls towards the gully fielder.
Keeps it in the channel outside off, the fifth stump line, Usman makes an easy leave.
FOUR! Round the wicket comes Anderson and gets too straight. It's drifting on the pads, Khawaja moves inside the line and clips it fine down the leg side for a boundary. Deft!
Broad with another bouncer, angling in towards the body of the batsman. Smith quickly arches back to let it be.
On a length and outside off, Steven lifts his bat to make another leave.
Good length delivery, wider outside off, Smith leans across before making a leave.
This time he gets on top of it and pulls it in front of square on the leg side for a single.

That surprised him actually! Broad bangs in a short one, a well-directed on from him. Khawaja is taken aback by it. The ball goes off the gloves and pops up towards the off side. On another day, it could have carried to the slip cordon or to the gully fielder. Not this time.
Ahead of a length, slanting it away a bit, Khawaja has it covered as he defends it down.
On middle and leg, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller in length, served on off, defended by prodding ahead.
Behind length and outside off, Usman stands tall to keep it out.
Touch fuller and outside off, blocked gently off the front foot.
Fuller and arrowing in on the pads, Steven gets across and flicks it through mid-wicket. Didn't time it well but still will get three runs.
Anderson bowls it on a back of a length, Smith gets across and with a high bat he defends it towards mid on.

Drinks are on the field now. Nothing to write home about as far as England are concerned. Both the batters are making merry, notching up their respective milestones. Khawaja got to his 6th Test ton, while his skipper romped over to another half century. Their stand is worth 151 runs, the deficit coming down to 9 runs over 100. Where does the respite for England come from now? This divine drinks interval?
Full on the stumps, hit towards mid-wicket.
Similar delivery, action replay.
This is full outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Poor line that. Broad strays on the pads with this length ball, easy pickings for Khawaja. He just tickles it away and the ball goes to the fine leg fence in a trice. Nice way to bring up the 150-run stand with his skipper. Also, he aggregates 2000 Test runs.
This time the drive is played to mid off, but doesn't beat the man there.
Steams in from round the wicket and bowls it full outside off. Khawaja drives this nicely to covers.
As expected, Stuart Broad will run in with this new cherry from the other end.
Smith plays it off the back foot towards square leg. A non-eventful over with this second new cherry, a maiden nevertheless.
Anderson has been around the good and short lengths so far in this over. Not ideal with the new ball, considering the speed with which he bowls.
Length ball outside off, Smith just lets it be.
Smith blocks by getting nicely behind this one.
This delivery is flicked towards mid-wicket.
Length ball on off, punched off the back foot towards mid off.
Anderson begins with a delivery on a length outside off. Smith covers his stumps and leaves it alone. Hint of movement there as the ball moves away nicely.
The second new ball is available and TAKEN STRAIGHTAWAY. James Anderson to have a go with it first up. Two slips in place. This is where things changed for England in their first essay.
Full outside off, left alone.
Yorker around off, digged out by Khawaja.

Wondered why Smith is so good with these on side flicks? Mark Taylor makes a nice observation. Smith's bat is held at an angle pointing towards mid on when he gets ready to face the ball. He just losens the grip and flicks the ball to the leg side when the ball appears. The initial angle of the bat helps him play that shot easily.
This is whipped away through square leg for one.
Another ball outside off, punched towards covers.
Punched off the back foot towards covers.

Good observation. The on-air commentators observe that England were in a similar position in the first innings. They were 228/3 before the second new ball was taken, from where things went downhill for them.
Khawaja works it down the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Steven rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
A bit short outside off, cut away through point for one.
Played with the spin through mid-wicket for a couple.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Khawaja dances down to this one and blocks it.
Mason strays on the pads again, Smith clips him away for a single.
This ball is pushed to the man at covers. Not a bad start for the young Tom.

Good point. Cameron Bancroft hasn't had a great run so far in this series and Khawaja, too, didn't have one till this one. Shane Warne on air opines that the youngster should be persisted with even after this series just to ensure that he gets the confidence and gets back among the runs. One can't always expect immediate results and patience is the key.
This is bowled aiming at the stumps, Uzzie defends it towards covers.
Full outside off, left alone.
Curran comes round the wicket and bowls a length ball around off. Khawaja stands tall and defends.
Angled in on the pads, worked through backward square leg for one. Smith moves up to 66, the trail gets down to 119.
Length ball in line of the stumps, defended towards mid on.
WIDE! Curran begins with a bumper that goes way over the batter's head. Smith ducks. Wide given.
Tom Curran to bowl now. He replaces Broad, who bowled just the one over. Shows England will opt for the second new cherry as soon as it will be available.
Short and spinning away outside off, Smith goes back and punches it through covers to retain strike.
Nicely flighted, Khawaja gets to the pitch of the ball and works it past mid-wicket for one.
Served around off, Usman hangs in his crease and defends with a lunge forward.
Sees this tossed up ball outside off, Khawaja comes down only to bunt it.
Crane continues over the wicket to the southpaw and tosses it outside off. Khawaja presents a straight bat face in defends.
A touch short on the pads, whipped away through square leg for a single.
The second new ball is 4 overs away. Meanwhile, Mason Crane comes in for a bowl. He lacked control towards the end of yesterday and one hopes, along with Warne, that he gets better.
Gets a soft outside edge towards gully as he looks to defend this.
Outside off, left alone.

Shane Warne was surprised this morning. He says that the early tactics from Anderson to bowl wide outside off from round the wicket seemed like backyard cricket for him. He admits to not have seen anything like that in the sport till that moment.
Full outside off, eased through covers for one.
Smith gets behind that and blocks it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On the pads, flicked away towards square leg.
Floated on off, defended with a straight bat.
Another delivery in line of the stumps, blocked.
UK has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Khawaja prods forward and defends this.
The batsman gets an inside edge and the ball hits him on the pads.

There it is! Usman Khawaja gets to his 6th Test hundred and he's pumped up. Why won't he be! This is his first Ashes hundred and with this he also ends a period where he has got starts but failed to convert it big. How does he get there? Gets a shortish ball outside off, Khawaja goes back and cuts it through point for a couple. Raises his bat in acknowledgement, unmindful of the fact that his skipper is seen lauding the effort and running towards him for a hug. The Australian trail comes down to 125 now.
Khawaja on 99 now. He'll face Ali now. Easier bowler? Maybe.
Broad makes Smith play this one with a full one on off. Steven blocks.
This is fuller outside off, but not good enough to make Smith play.
Another one outside off, Smith just lets it be.
Hurled outside off, left alone.
Full on off, defended off the front foot.

FOUR! Textbook, sit back and enjoy, says Bill Lawry on this one. Hardly do we see back foot drives being played in this modern era and here is Smith with the same. Gets a delivery that is relatively full outside off, he gets his back leg across and drives it through covers. Result, a boundary.
Stuart Broad into the attack now, replacing Anderson. After Bancroft's wicket early yesterday, he has failed to add another to his kitty.
Bowled on the pads, worked to fine leg for one.
Khawaja moves on 99 by guiding this to the right of point.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Not the best of balls this. Ali serves this short and wide outside off, Khawaja stays back and cuts it powerfully in front of square. The ball speeds away to the fence to take UK to 98.
Flat outside off, left alone.
Tucked away through square leg for a single that takes him to 94.
Full outside off, driven towards mid off.
This ball is driven towards mid off for one. This is Smith's 2000th run against England in Tests.
Outside off, left alone.

For once, we can say this - Smith is foxed by Anderson. He stands in a wide-stanced position anticipating another full and wide delivery. What does he get? A spearing yorker at 138 kph. Thankfully for Smith, it is not in line of the stumps and before he could adjust and get some bat to that, it makes contact with the front pad that is outside the line of the leg stick. The ball rolls to the slip cordon then. Well bowled, Jimmy.
Full outside off, driven towards mid off.
Another forward defense to end the over. A maiden for Mo.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated full outside off, driven towards covers.
Khawaja lunges forward and blocks this one.

What's that? A chance? Don't think so. Khawaja gets down to this tossed up ball and looks to go inside out. Ends up getting an inside edge onto his pads and it lobs towards silly mid off. Perhaps it just bumped before lobbing off the pads.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
This length ball is worked through backward square leg for a brace. Smith moves to 56 and the stand to 121.
Well outside off, left alone.
Full outside off, Smith exposes his stumps, gets across and blocks it with a straight bat. Never plays according to the books, does this guy. Yet he scores runs and that's what matters.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
This is full outside off from round the wicket, Smith just lets it be.
Fuller on middle and leg, worked away through square leg for one. Uzzie moves to 93.
A silly mid off in place.
This ball is played towards mid on.
SS defends it from within the crease.

FOUR! Nicely struck. Ali tosses this wide outside off, Smith reaches out to this and whips it through covers. Yes, he whips it - one of his typical wristy shots through covers. The fielder from covers chases it down, slides and seems to have done well. The umpire goes upstairs just to be sure and finds that the player was in contact with the ball and the ropes at the same time and thus it is a boundary, the first one of the day.
Nicely played. Khawaja picks up his first run of the day by getting down the track and placing this through covers.

A milestone early in the day. No prizes for guessing who, Steven Smith. He just flicks this off his pads and picks up three as the ball rolls towards fine leg to bring up his 23rd HALF CENTURY IN TESTS. He has largely been untroubled yet again and continues to be England's nemesis on the tour.
Ali begins with a floated delivery on off, turned to mid-wicket.
Surprising move this. Moeen Ali to begin the day from the other end. Perhaps more purchase is expected to be extracted from the surface and hence this move.
This is full outside off, left alone by Usman. Tidy start for both sides.
Jimmy comes over the wicket to Khawaja and bowls it full around off. The batter just pushes it back defensively.
This ball is similar to the second delivery, turned through mid-wicket for one.
Full and well outside off, Steven gets behind that and pushes it towards covers.
On a length angling away from the off stump, Smith gets across and clips it wristily through square leg for a brace. First runs for the day already. Hard to keep this guy quiet, isn't it?
Strange start. Anderson runs in from round the wicket and bowls it full outside off. Smith covers the stumps and lets it go.

All the off-cricket action is done now. Time for the sport to take centre stage now. The unbeaten pair of Khawaja and Smith walks out to the middle. It will be James Anderson to begin the day first up. 13 overs to go before the second new ball is available. A slip and a short cover stand in position for Smith, who will face the first delivery. Here we go...

A huge pink cloth, having the photo of Jane McCgrath, is held up on the ground. It is due to her that the McGrath foundation has come up to support the cause of breast cancer. The former pacer himself is very actively involved in promoting this noble cause. The response that they receive for the same is massive. Everything right from the players' caps to the caps that the security forces are wearing are pink in color. Now the Aussies walk out, shake hands with Glenn McGrath and hand over their signed pink baggy caps to him. Even the English players do the same now. Lovely to see players from both the sides unite in this noble cause.

Today is Day 3, the Pink day at the SCG. Everything would be rosy-colored to commemorate the Jane McGrath day. This is in honor of former pacer Glenn McGrath's wife, who had succumbed to breast cancer. England, so far, have lacked inspiration and would need to lift themselves up quickly. The hosts are behind by 153 runs and thus, the visitors still have plenty in their bank to play with. Will Joe Root's men manage to turn it around today? Or will Smith's and Australia's juggernaut roll on? We'll find out in just a bit.

How do we get past the enigma called Steven Smith, this might be the thought in the English camp as we enter the third day of this final Ashes Test. Australia find themselves at a comfortable position, thanks to fifties from David Warner and Usman Khawaja. The latter is well on course to get a triple figure score in this format after a gap of over a year and 8 Tests while the Aussie skipper is just 6 short of raking up another 50-plus score.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

An involving day's play ends. Day 3 is often reckoned as the moving day in a Test and we would love to see what happens tomorrow. It promises to be a day full of thrilling action and we would love to have your company then. There is a tweet from Cricket Australia that confirms play will start tomorrow at 1030 local time (1130 GMT). Do join us then. Meanwhile, you can switch over and catch another exciting Test that we have on the cards where India take on South Africa in the series opener in Cape Town. See you tomorrow, ta-ta, take care!

One wonders what wrong did England do. Their bowlers weren't as awry as the figures suggest. They were successful in inducing numerous edges but those failed to carry to the fielders. Crane was a disappointment on a surface that aided spin. He was losing his run up continuously and needs to get that sorted before he can settle into a nice rhythm. Anderson and Broad bowled their hearts out but have only one wicket to show. This is after their lower order did well to post a score that seemed decent at the end of the innings. Broad and Curran did well with the bat as well apart from Malan, who failed to add much to his overnight score.

The Australian opener says that Khawaja's temperament was fantastic and he seemed to be in full flow. Adds further that he has a fantastic hand-eye coordination, wonderful timing and he models himself on Lara. Lauds him for playing well against Ali. Khawaja was irritated about not converting the starts but has rectified that with this knock, he reveals. Admits to being shocked at England not sending in the nightwatchman last night. Adds that their bowlers reaped rewards for their toil on the field. About the catches that have gone down, he agrees that's not a good thing and the team is not happy with that. Jokes that Smith drops catches that come straight to him but takes the difficult ones. About Hazlewood's dropped catch, he says these can be difficult ones, to which Healy and Nicholas, on a lighter note, tell him to not make excuses for his teammate. About Cummins, he states that he is an athlete who has been good at home as well as away. Admits bowling well to the opposition tail and states that it was a collective effort on their part. Singles out Lyon for his significant contribution with the ball and on the field. He wasn't aware of being on the cusp of scoring four consecutive hundreds at the SCG but adds that he doesn't chase records. Reckons that he is trying to move late and is working hard in the nets. Reasons that he had to change his gameplan owing to the different field placements that England have had against him. Ends saying that he is running out of superlatives to describe Smith, who faces a lot of balls in the nets and blows away everyone with the way he trains. Goes to the extent of naming him as the 'New-age Bradman'.

Australia's session, no doubt, and they even take the day's honors. They are just 153 runs behind England's score and one can assume that England would already be feeling low about the situation that they are in right now. Warner and Khawaja set about with the task after they lost Bancroft pretty early. The former departed soon after his fifty, something he might be ruing after seeing the latter go about with his task. Khawaja is just 9 short of his ton and has an in-form Smith, who has just passed 6000 Test runs, for company. Mark Nicholas and Ian Healy catch up with David Warner for a long chat and lets have a look at what he had to say...
Flatter on the stumps, Khawaja goes back and safely sees the day off. That's STUMPS! Australia TRAIL by 153 runs!
Floated outside off, driven nicely straight to the man stationed at covers.
Flatter on the pads, kept out from the crease.
Now he has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Khawaja seems to want it today. Goes back and cuts this one fiercely but fails to beat point.

FOUR! Almost seems like the moment Cook notched up his hundred at the MCG. It was the last over of the day then, Smith came and offered him freebies to help him. Here Root comes in and bowls it short around off. Khawaja goes back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Moves to 91 now. A century tonight?

'Rooooooooooot' goes the crowd as it sees Joe Root come into the attack. This is the final over of the day. Is he the man with the golden arm? Remember, he picked a set Warner up in the previous game off his second ball.
This is a yorker, Smith digs it out back towards the bowler.
Floated around off, Khawaja looks to defend. But the ball goes off the outside edge past slip for a single.
Smith flicks this off the pads and gets to the other end.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Served on the pads, clipped away fine on the leg side for a brace. That brings up the 100-run stand between these two.
Flatter ball in line of the stumps, punched back to mid on.
Floated outside off, eased towards covers.
This is bowled around middle and leg, SS gets down and sweeps it through backward square leg for one. Moves to 41, trail comes down to 161.
Straight outside off, Smith doesn't put bat to that.
This one is wristed to the man at mid-wicket.
Quicker on the stumps, blocked towards short leg.
Loopy ball outside off at 85 kph, Smith turns it to mid-wicket.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Shorter outside off, carved through covers for one.
Wow! Khawaja with a quick single? Yep, you read it right. He pats it towards mid off and scurries to the other end. There is a missed throw at the bowler's end but he seemed to be safe.
Khawaja gets down the track and dead-bats it.
Floated in line of the stumps, Khawaja presents a straight bat face in blocking that.
Flatter outside off, slapped through covers for one.
Mason Crane is brought back for another spell.

One can't help but envy seeing the time that Smith seems to have to play his shots. This is just a touch shorter outside off, Smith goes back and cuts it through point and gets three runs for the effort.

Bowled on a flatter trajectory, spinning down leg. Smith fails to flick it and even Bairstow misses collecting that. The ball rolls towards third man and seeing this the Aussie skipper wants a run but Khawaja doesn't respond. Bill Lawry says that he has probably dozed off.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Eased through covers to get to the other end.
Well done, Joe! Another edge played with soft hands that doesn't carry. Root at first slip, had to dive to his right to stop that. Saves a certain couple.
Flat and outside off, Usman punches it towards covers.

Short of length and well wide of off, Smith gets his right leg across and punches it on the up through covers. Beats the man there who attempts to stop it with a dive. A couple added to Smith's tally who moves to 35.
On a length well outside off, Steven watches it go and thud into the keeper's gloves.
Full and outside off, Smith leaves it alone.

Length ball outside off, punched off the back foot through covers. Wait, was the initial call from Khawaja but he had done well to get it through the gap. It races down the hill there and a treble results.
Length ball on middle and leg, clipped towards mid-wicket where Stoneman puts in the dive and stops.
Jimmy steams in and lands it on a length angling across Uzzie. He just lets it be.
This is angled in, tucked to square leg for one.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up around off and middle, Khawaja comes down the track and bunts it down.
Served outside off, pushed towards point.
Ali has beaten Khawaja's bat numerous times and does so yet again. Tosses it just outside off, draws Usman's defensive bat and spins the other way to go into the keeper's gloves.
Floated outside off, eased through mid-wicket for a single.
Moeen Ali to roll his arm over.
Full on off, stonewalled off the front foot.
On a length around middle and off, Usman looks to punch it but gets it off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
Anderson changes his angle and comes over the wicket. Bowls it on a length in line of the stumps. Khawaja defends showing the full face of the bat.
This is outside off on a fuller length, Khawaja presents a straight bat in defending that towards covers.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full outside off, Khawaja fails to beat the man at covers with the drive.
Khawaja drives this through covers to register his highest Test score at the SCG.
This is the wrong one, worked away with the spin through mid-wicket for a single.
Another false start... Crane really needs to sort his issues out. Not good this for a spinner.
Served outside off, reverse swept to deep point. Curran does well to save a run for his side.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floated outside off, Khawaja gets down to sweep. Does so but it strikes Stoneman at short leg. The ball deflects to mid on.
Tossed up outside off, driven through covers to get to the other end.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full outside off, driven to cover.
Another one outside off, left alone.
On a length on off, Khawaja goes back to block.
Another ball outside off, Usman lets it go unharmed.
Outside off, left alone.
Root is seen wearing a helmet as he is standing ahead at second slip.

Floated on off, clipped through square leg for one. Crane is yet to bowl a maiden in this innings. Here again he concedes a run off the last ball of the over. Needs to exert more control on the proceedings.
Khawaja defends with his bat in front of his pads.
Khawaja works it off his pads towards mid-wicket.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Floated outside off, Usman gets down to sweep but wears it on the front pad. No appeal made as the impact is well outside off.
Big turn. Crane pitches this well outside off but the ball spins in big. Khawaja looks to defend but it goes off the pad towards square leg for nothing.
Similar delivery and sequence of action like the previous ball.
Fuller on off, defended from the crease.

Excellent running between the wickets. Whether he is running for his runs or for others', Smith does his best to steal an extra one. This is bowled a touch fuller outside off, Khawaja guides it past gully with soft hands. Gets three runs as a result of good running.
Angling in, UK plays it towards mid-wicket.
Full ball aiming at the off stump, Khawaja presents a straight bat in defense.
Comes round the wicket and bowls it full outside off, Usman points his bat skywards to let that go.
James Anderson is back on.
Smith hits this one with the turn to the man at covers.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Another false start...
Khawaja looks to go over the top but gets it off the inner half towards deep square leg for one.
The batsman works it down the leg side.

Slight mix up. Khawaja gets down and places this one towards mid on. Takes start as if to take a run but then decides against it. Smith had responded initially but then he had to run around the bowler to make his ground. All safe in the end as the throw is at the keeper's end.
Floated outside off from round the wicket, Khawaja comes down the track and takes it on the full. Hits it straight to mid on.
Another dot ball to end the over. It is a touch fuller, Smith blocks.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Smith gets forward and blocks it with a straight bat.
On a length on off, defended from the crease.

FOUR! Another edge, another boundary, more agony! Broad runs in and delivers a leg cutter around off, the ball straightens after pitching, Smith offers a dead bat in defense but the movement on the occasion means that the outside edge is taken. It flies down low towards first slip but doesn't carry to Cook there. Bairstow realises this early and puts in the dive but it is far for him as well. The ball races away to the fence behind after going in between the two of them. Broad, understandably, is frustrated and vents it out to let everybody know. The key there was Smith playing it with soft hands, which meant that the ball wouldn't carry to the slip cordon.
Angling in to Usman from round the wicket, he taps it towards mid-wicket and gets across to the other end.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up outside off, Smith allows it to turn and lets it go.
Floated outside off, Khawaja gets down and reverse sweeps it through point and gets to the other end.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On the pads, flicked round the corner from the crease.

There it is! 6000 Test runs for Steven Smith and he is the second quickest to the mark behind Sir Don Bradman. He has got there in 111 Test innings, equalling Gary Sobers' mark. How does he get there? By pulling a short delivery offered by Crane to deep backward square leg for a single. Just a small raise of the bat to acknowledge the feat.
This one is defended towards point.
Reverse swing? Broad is seen running with the ball covered.
Length ball outside off, punched towards covers.
Broad comes in from round the wicket and bowls it full outside off. Left alone by UK.
A leg gully, mid-wicket and mid on in place apart from a deep backward square leg.
Short on the stumps, pulled away to fine leg for one.
On a length on off, defended towards cover-point.

FOUR! More agony for England! Here is another edge from the willow of an Australian that doesn't go to the hands of an English fielder. Broad bowls it full outside off, Smith goes for the full-blooded cover drive. Gets a thick outside edge past the second slip fielder for a boundary. Smith stands on 24 runs, 5998 Test runs to his credit.

Drinks are on the field! Australia have done well to not lose a wicket after tea. Smith and Khawaja both have settled with the latter registering his fifty. England are looking really flat. Who will produce that spark to bring them back into the game?
Turning a touch, stabbed off the back foot towards point.
Quicker one outside off, Khawaja pads it away. Root at first slip fluffs but they can't run as Khawaja didn't offer any shot.
The batsman has been struck on the pads as he looked to play that off the front foot.
Gets forward and eases it through covers for a single.
Did that carry? Nope! Floats it up around middle and off, Smith comes down the track to defend but the ball spins away, takes the outside edge and it falls just short of Root at first slip.
Outside off, turning in, Khawaja gets into the position early and nails the reverse sweep to deep point for a single.
In the channel outside off, pretty harmless, Steven lifts his bat to make an assured leave.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Fires it wider outside off, Smith shoulders his arms.
Bangs in a short ball on middle and off, Smith ducks under it.
Fuller in length and outside off, driven towards the man at cover.
Back of a length delivery to begin with, Smith defends it off the back foot.
Stuart Broad is back into the attack.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! That's a gift wrapped with red ribbon on it! A juicy full toss on middle, Smith murders the pull through mid-wicket for a boundary.
What's wrong Crane? Twice he misses his run up. Looks that he is not finding his rhythm...
Full toss outside off, UK nails the sweep through mid-wicket for one.

Almost takes the wicket! Crane goes around the wicket, pitches it on the rough outside off, Khawaja plants his front foot across and half-heartedly goes after it. He is late to take his bat out and the edge is found. It goes wide of Root at first slip. In fact right between Bairstow and the English skipper. Two taken. Strangely, Root has placed himself wider as Crane is a leg spinner and if the edge is induced, it won't go wider.
Loopy full toss, dipping in, Smith whips it away to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up delivery outside off, Smith presses forward to kill it into the ground.
Fuller in length and in the corridor outside off, Usman Khawaja ignores.
In the probing zone outside off, Usman lifts his bat to let it be.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Wider outside off, Usman shoulders his arms.
On a length and in the channel on off, Usman looks to defend but gets an edge which falls well short of Root at second slip who stops it with his left palm.
Curran comes from around the wicket and hurls it on off, Khawaja prods forward in defense.
Leg break, pitching on middle, turning away, Smith leans forward and drives it towards cover.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Comes down the track and pushes it towards cover for a quick single. Brings up the 50-run stand as well.
Leans across to flick it with the turn towards mid-wicket.
FOUR! Thumped! Khawaja makes good use of the feet to this flighted ball and goes bang down the ground for a boundary.
Around middle and leg, Khawaja comes down the track to flick but misses as the ball goes off the pads and falls short of Stoneman at short leg.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Good length delivery outside off, defended off the back foot comfortably.
Outside off, it's a loopy full toss, another drive and finds the man at cover. Smith knows he has missed out on that one.
Driven straight to the fielder at cover.
Fuller again and angling in, Smith drives it back down the track as Curran stops it in his followthrough.
Fuller in length and outside off, driven nicely only to find the man at cover.
Just short of the man at short leg! Around middle, turning back in, Khawaja goes back and tucks it. The man at short leg crouches low and tries to take it but the ball still falls short of him.
Short and outside off, Khawaja goes back and cuts it to deep backward point for a couple.
Around middle and leg, flicked towards mid-wicket for a single.
Makes room and drives it through covers for a single.
Comes down the track and jams it back to the bowler who collects. England feel it's caught and bowled but it's a bump ball.
Floats it up on the stumps, Khawaja blocks it out from the crease.
A tidy over from Curran! Drags his length back, Smith defends it off the back foot and calls for a new pair of gloves immediately.
Very full outside off, almost a yorker, Smith digs it out towards cover.
Back of a length ball outside off, punched nicely off the back foot towards the cover fielder.
Gets right behind the line and shows a straight bat.
Tad short and outside off, Smith walks across and defends it down solidly.

Edgyyyy! Curran bowls it fuller and wider outside off, Khawaja goes fishing after it. Gets a thick edge which flies on the bounce to the left of the gully fielder. The man there gets a bit of hand to it which slows it down. A single collected.
Comes down the track does Khawaja and nearly yorks himself. Still manages to dig it out towards the cover region which allows him to keep strike.
Pitching on leg, turning down, Khawaja leans forward to flick but misses.
That's the thing with the leggies. They will surely bowl one short. Here it is, Smith goes back and crunches it to deep point for a single.
Tossed up leg break outside off, turning further away, Smith is happy to leave it alone.
A bit too full on the stumps, blocked down gently.
Around middle and leg, Smith pushes it towards cover. Comes halfway down the track in search of a single but Khawaja sends him back.
A confident stride forward to this full ball from Khawaja as he blocks it back down the track.
Fuller and angling away, staying a bit low too. Khawaja has it covered as he makes a leave.
Good length ball on off, defended with soft hands as the ball rolls towards mid off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Once again flicks it from middle stump and sends it towards backward square leg this time. A single taken.
Gets across, it's full on middle and leg, Smith flicks it through mid-wicket for a double.

FOUR! That has to be a boundary! Good effort from Curran though! Fuller delivery outside off, Khawaja leans forward and drives it through square of the wicket on the off side. Tom in the deep runs across to his right, puts in a dive but makes contact with the rope when he had the ball in the hand. Replays confirm the same. Usman moves to 55.
Stays back and pushes it towards point.
A bit short on middle, tucked towards the leg side.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
No ball! Tossed up on off, driven back to the bowler. Crane oversteps and will have to reload it.
Around middle and leg, worked towards the leg side.

A cry for an LBW! Crane starts off with a leg spinner, pitching on middle and leg and turning further down. Usman comes forward to defend but misses and gets hit on the pads. They appeal but umpire shakes his head. Bairstow and Root come down to the pitch to have a word with the bowler. But they don't take the review. Replays show the impact is outside leg.
Double change as debutant Mason Crane is brought back to roll his arm over.
Smith once again drives it in the same region. Shows patience of not going after it.
Seam up delivery on the stumps, driven straight to Anderson at silly mid on.
Length delivery, nipping away a shade, Smith tries to defend but this one stays a tad low too. Takes an outside edge which evades the man at gully and they come back for a couple.
Back of a length outside off, a bit of extra bounce but Smith adjusts to keep it out.
Another short one outside off, Smith taps it towards the off side.
Shortish on middle and off, pushed towards Anderson at silly mid on.
Tom Curran is back!
Short outside off, cut towards the man at point.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

SIX! Down the track and banggggg! That's some shot to bring up your fifty! Khawaja will be itching to get a big one now. This is his third fifty in the series, 11th overall. Ali bowls a flighted ball around middle, Usman wears his dancing shoes, gets to the pitch of the ball and smacks it straight down the ground for a biggie. Superb!
Takes a stride forward and pushes it towards cover.
That's off the meat! Smith gets down to sweep but it hits the pad of Stoneman at short leg and deflects further towards square leg. A single taken.
Tossed up outside off, Smith comes down the track to flick but is early into the shot. Gets a leading edge towards cover.
Opens the bat face and defends it towards point.
Attacking the stumps does Anderson, Khawaja gets across and defends.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Michael Clarke on air analyzes Smith's scoring chart. It shows that about 166 and 136 runs that Smith has scored in this series have come through cover and mid-wicket respectively. It's only through mid off where the Aussie skipper has the least no. of runs which reads just 16. He wants Root to take that man out from mid off and place him either at catching cover or mid-wicket to block Smith from scoring runs through his favoured regions...
On middle and leg, worked through backward square leg for a single.
Pitches it further up outside off, blocked solidly again.
Anderson continues from over the wicket and hurls it outside off, Smith defends it off the back foot.
This delivery is cut away towards point.
Flatter on the stumps, defended from the crease.
FOUR! Brilliant use of the feet here. Khawaja has walked out from the break with a positive mindset. He charges down to this one and whips it past mid on for a boundary.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
This one is turned through mid-wicket for a single.
Floated in line of the stumps, blocked from the crease.
Full on off, driven to mid off.
Usman blocks it off the front foot onto the ground.

Mindset. It matters a lot in sport. Ian Healy jokes saying whether England would be wondering Smith's due for a failure and bowl accordingly. To this Clarke replies saying if they think on those lines, they'll be in trouble. Cannot take anything for granted in sport.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Anderson pitches this further than the previous one, Khawaja covers his stumps and lets it go.

FOUR! Look at the Hot Spot to see where Khawaja got it on the bat. Absolutely middled that one. Anderson lands it on a length around middle, Khawaja pulls it with some authority through square leg for a boundary.
Lands it on a length around off and middle, Usman punches it back.
James Anderson will continue.
Short in length, pulled to the man at square leg for nothing.
Floated outside off, turned to the man at mid on.
Bit more air given on this one, Khawaja lunges forward in defense. But he gets an inside edge towards square leg for one.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
This is bowled in line of the stumps, Usman goes back and defends it with a straight bat.
Flatter ball on the stumps, Khawaja goes back and keeps it out towards mid-wicket.

We are back for the final session. Steven Smith and Usman Khawaja will resume the battle. Australia trail by 250 runs and we have around 30 overs remaining in the day. Moeen Ali will kick off the proceedings. Let's roll...
... Day 2, Session 3 ...

Right then! Steven Smith is at it again. Khawaja is unbeaten on 36 and needs to carry on. England would very well know that if they manage to remove that man who has just arrived, they can surely gain the upper hand in this Test. Their bowling has been relatively flat with only Anderson and Broad finding their rhythm. Ali has been good today but at the same time has offered freebies to nullify his effort. Debutant Crane didn't impress much but it would be interesting to see how he fares further. An exciting final session awaits! Join us back shortly...

Had it not been for the wicket of David Warner, this would have been Australia's session all the way. But the honours are shared for now. After getting bundled out in the first session, England got a perfect start through Broad who removed Bancroft for a duck. However, the pair of Warner and Khawaja weathered the storm with the former looking really solid. The opener scored a gritty fifty but just before the break, Anderson outfoxed him with a lovely off cutter to make sure the southpaw doesn't get a big one at his home ground.
Shortish on leg, helped with a pull to deep backward square leg for a single. TEA ON DAY 2!
Length ball on middle, turned toward mid-wicket.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Nice way to open the account! Fuller ball, a half volley from Jimmy. Smith leans across and caresses it through extra cover. Gets three for doing so.
Driven towards mid off for nothing.
Fuller in length and outside off, Smith presses forward to defend but gets an inside edge as the ball rolls towards mid on.
Fuller on off, Khawaja mistimes his drive towards cover.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! There to be hit! Ali throws it short, it's wider outside off, enough room for Khawaja to pounce on it. He jumps back and slaps it a bit squarer on the off side to pick up a boundary. The commentator on air jokes saying that this is the tough time for any batsman in this Ashes as most of them have departed in the mid 30s.
Gets down and across to paddle scoop it towards fine leg for a couple of runs.
Flatter through the air, UK hangs back in defense.
Floated delivery outside off, Khawaja prods forward to block it out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fuller in length and just outside off, dealt off the front foot by Smith.
Steven Smith strides out to bat next. Huge cheers from the crowd as the Aussie run-machine walks out. The home town boy is at it again. What will we see from him today?

OUT! Got him... Yes, gone! No hundred for David Warner, shouts an excited Mark Taylor on air. What a classical delivery from Anderson to break this stubborn stand! He has his right hand up as he races towards the slip cordon. He smartly tries an off cuter that pitches on middle and off and moves away slightly. Warner is neither fully forward nor backward and in the end has a tame poke at it. Gets a feather and it travels low to Bairstow behind who accepts the catch. A solid fifty for Warner but he walks back dejected. England rejoice!
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They manage to come back for the second.
Fullish on off, pushed towards mid off.
Good length delivery on middle and off, Warner is happy to sit back and defend.
Floated delivery outside off, Khawaja prods forward in defense. A good over from Ali.
Loopy ball outside off, defended into the ground.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Slower through the air outside off, Khawaja comes forward to defend but the ball turns away to beat the outside edge.
Around middle and leg, worked towards mid-wicket.

In the air... just wide of Cook at silly mid off. Tossed up delivery outside off, Khawaja comes down the track and looks to chip it over the off side. It's just wide of Cook at silly mid off who dives to his right with his hand out but the ball evades him and rolls towards mid off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Hangs back and shows a straight blade.

Ohhhhhh! That was close! Anderson angles it away on a length outside off, gets it to seam away with some bounce. Warner tries to hit on the up but is beaten all ends up. David smiles and appreciates it as well.
Fuller and slanted away outside off, defended off the front foot.

Mark Taylor on air makes a fair point. He agrees that Australia have got a good start after an early stutter but feels Khawaja should start to score freely now. The more he hangs back, the higher is the possibility of him getting out. The Englishmen were guilty of doing just that. Warner on the other end is keeping the scorecard ticking and Usman Khawaja should think on the same lines...
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Length delivery, curling back in a bit, Khawaja works it off the inner half through backward square leg for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Darted on middle and leg, wristed towards mid-wicket.
Drifting in on middle and leg, Warner gets an inside edge on the pads.
Makes some room and pushes it towards the cover region.

FOUR! Warner has flayed this one! Ali drops it short and it's wider outside off. David doesn't miss out on this as he rocks back in a jiffy and cracks it square of the wicket on the off side for a boundary.
Tossed up outside off, defended into the ground.
There is some issue with the ball. It's not going through the 8-shaped gauge and the umpires are getting it changed...
Shortish on middle, punched back to Anderson. A maiden on return for Anderson.
Length ball, closer to the off stump line, dealt off the back foot by Usman.

Root is standing a few steps ahead from where he was originally standing waiting for the edge to come. Ian Healy on air reckons, the edge that didn't carry a while ago would have carried had Root positioned himself here at that time...
Back of a length delivery on middle, defended from within the crease.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Fifty for David Warner, his 27th in Tests! He continues to impress at his home ground. Gets a length delivery and tucks it through square leg for a single. Gets a warm applause from the crowd and he shows the bat to the dressing room. Another big one on the cards?
Fuller in length and outside off, Warner eases the drive towards mid off.
James Anderson is back into the attack.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Out of nowhere! Moeen Ali floats it up around off, Khawaja comes charging down the track but isn't completely to the pitch of the ball. Drags it off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

A huge shout for an LBW, not given! Loopy ball outside off, Khawaja gets across to play the paddle sweep but seems to have missed it and gets hit on the pads. They keep appealing but umpire turns it down. Root is interested in reviewing it but doesn't get the desired support. Replays show there was a thin feather which would have saved Khawaja and also the impact would have been umpire's call.
After bowling full on the previous ball, Moeen bowls it short outside off to which Warner rocks back and punches it towards cover-point for a single. On 49 now.

FOUR! Beautifully done! Amazingly timed as well! Ali tosses it up outside off, Warner makes room and drills it exquisitely to beat the dive of the man at extra cover. Away she races for a boundary and Warner moves to 48.
Good length ball, in the probing channel outside off, UK is happy to block those.
Broad goes fuller, it's on off, Usman presses forward to push it towards mid off.
Angling across Khawaja who has it covered before making a leave.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Good length delivery on off, answered with a straight bat.
Fuller and around off, Khawaja closes the face of the bat and works it towards the man at mid-wicket.
Gets forward and defends it off the inner half towards square leg.
Spinning away from a length outside off, slapped towards the point fielder.
Flatter delivery outside off, Warner punches it towards point.
Fuller outside off, driven towards mid off.

Drops it short and outside off, Khawaja chops it behind point. It beats the man there and the batsmen start to sprint. In fact it's Warner who is really quick and calls for the third. They take three in the end.

That stayed really, really low! Quicker through the air, fired outside off, Khawaja goes back to defend but the ball doesn't rise at all. Beats the edge too and Bairstow behind the stumps collects it and takes the bails off.
Moeen Ali is back on.
Good length ball on middle and off, Warner covers the line and defends it.
Leans forward and defends it right under his eye line.

Edged just short of Root at second slip! Good bowling from Broad! He steams in and angles it away on a length just outside off. The line is such that Warner had to play at it and the ball jags away a bit to take the edge. Luckily for him the ball dips in front of Root at second slip before the English skipper takes it. He then gets up and throws the ball in disgust towards mid off.
Length delivery, close to the off stump line, blocked out.
Offers a bit of width and it's on the shorter length. Warner cracks one through the line but the packed off side field means that it goes straight to point.
Good length ball on the pads, tucked away through square leg for a single.
Very full outside off, UK crouches a bit and squeezes it out past Cook at first slip for a single to keep strike.
Seeing the flight, Khawaja steps out of the crease, takes it on the full and drives it hard only to find the man at cover. Anderson dives to his right to make a good stop.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Turning back in on middle and leg, Khawaja comes forward to defend but gets an inside edge on the pads but the ball dies down safely.
More flight from Mason, pushed into the off side.
Loops it up around middle, Khawaja comes down the track and bunts it back to Crane who picks it up and mimes a throw back at the striker's end.
Another one on the same length, blocked safely off the back foot towards cover.
Hits the length, it's served outside off, tapped off the back foot.
Shortish and angling away a touch from over the wicket, David hangs back to defend it down.
Another one strangled on the pads, easily clipped towards fine leg for a single.
Back of a length delivery on middle, turned towards mid-wicket off the back foot.
Broad comes from around the wicket and strays on the pads, Khawaja walks across and clips it towards deep backward square leg for a brace.
Change in bowling. Stuart Broad is back into the attack. Bowled just 4 overs in his opening spell and got a wicket of Bancroft. Can he provide another breakthrough?
Bowls the googly on middle but the length is short which allows Warner to go back and counter it.
Keeps it fuller on the stumps, defended into the ground by David.
Khawaja skips down the track and nudges it with the spin through mid-wicket for a single.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for one.
Leans forward and blocks it out watchfully.
Nice loop on this occasion. Warner is up for the task, he makes room and places it wide of the man at cover for a couple.
Warner comes down the track and hits it back down the ground. Ali gets a bit of hand to it as he parries it towards mid off. The duo take the single.
This time Khawaja drives one through the cover region to get off strike.

Good point from Shane Warne. An off spinner is likely to pick wickets when he gets the ball to drift. And for that you need to give revs on the ball. Something, Ali is failing to do in this series. During the English summer he was successful as he was seen doing the same. Whatever maybe the reason, you need to give it a nice loop to trouble the batsmen...
Makes a bit of room and eases it through cover for a single.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region.
Loopy delivery outside off, blocked off the front foot.
Close! Quicker one on off, Warner makes room and cuts it from off stump towards point.

An appeal for an LBW! England think of the review but decide not to. Flighted ball around middle and leg, Usman comes forward and with his bat and pad close together. The ball hits the pads but not sure if it hit that first. They appeal but nothing from the umpire. Maybe, Khawaja got an inside edge there.
Pitches it fuller, provides some loop, Warner whips it wide of Broad at mid on for a single.
Khawaja goes deep in the crease and tucks it past short leg for a single.
Quicker one one leg, spinning further down leg, Warner clips it off the inner half past short leg for a single.
Around middle, turning in, Warner covers the sticks to defend it down.
Slower leg break outside off, turning in a bit, Warner stands back to stab it away.
Floated delivery outside off, Khawaja presses forward to keep it out.
Pushes it quicker through the air around off, Usman stands back in defense.
This time David gets it past the man at cover-point for a single.
Flatter one on off, Warner cuts it off the back foot but finds the man at cover-point.
Floats it up on the stumps, Warner defends it comfortably off the front foot.
Fuller in length and angling in around middle and leg, Khawaja leans across and clips it past short leg for a single.

Time for drinks. England believed that they could make further inroads when they had Bancroft early. The ensuing period saw some disciplined efforts with the ball from Broad and Anderson. However, Khawaja and Warner have managed to keep them at bay and now are starting to get a move on. Can England manage to break this stand and make further inroads?
This is landed around off, pushed back towards the bowler.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Short and wide outside off, cut away through point for a couple.
Tossed up on off, driven towards covers.

50-run partnership between Warner and Khawaja is up. They have steadied the ship yet again after an early fall of a wicket. Crane bowls this down the leg side, Usman just lets it be. Bairstow fails to collect it cleanly and a bye results.
Floated outside off, stabbed through covers for one.
This one is knocked through covers for a single.
Warner stays in the crease and blocks it solidly.
Served in line of the stumps, turned towards square leg.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
This is on the pads, worked away to fine leg for one.
Floated on a fuller length on off and middle, Khawaja lunges forward in defense.
Change of ends for Moeen Ali. Meanwhile, Anderson was seen talking to Crane after the end of the previous over. Gives him a high five after the small talk.
A short ball to end the over, punched through wide mid off for a brace. 3 runs of Crane's first over in Test cricket, not a bad one.
Flatter on the stumps, Warner goes back and defends it towards point.
Floated on the stumps, Warner presents a straight bat in forward defense.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flatter down the leg side, left alone.
Crane begins with a half-tracker in line of the stumps, Khawaya goes back and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for one.
Mason Crane is brought into the attack. He is making his debut and would like to make the right noises first up.

FOUR! Three boundaries in four balls to end the over. Warner is on the charge and the young Curran bears the brunt of that. This is bowled on a length around off, Warner punches it through mid off. The fielder there puts in the dive but fails to get any hand to that. 12 runs off this over, Warner moves to 30.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.

FOUR! Now this is overcorrection. On the previous ball, he had given enough width to the batsman, now he straightens his line a bit too much. All Warner has to do is get some bat on that, which he does with a flick. There is no protection in the deep on the leg side and the ball goes away to the fence.
FOUR! Curran isn't being disciplined with his stuff so far. Overpitches this outside off, Warner leans ahead and drives it through covers for a boundary. Wonderful balance maintained by him there.
Fuller around off, driven towards mid off.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Served in line of the stumps, defended with a straight bat.
Khawaja goes back and slaps it but straight to the cover fielder.

You hit me for a boundary, I get back at you with a ripper, says Moeen Ali with this jaffa. He gets this one to pitch around off and just spin past the bat that is poken by Khawaja as he attempts to block this one.

FOUR! Well played. The key to play against spin is to make good use of the feet and that is exactly what Khawaja has done here. He sees the tossed up ball on offer and gets down the track. Blasts it past Ali. The mid off fielder is pretty wide and has no chance of preventing the boundary.
Warner pats this one towards mid off and gets to the other end.
First run off Ali's bowling. He tosses it up on a fuller length around off, eased down to long off for one.
On the pads, turned through square leg for a single.
Outside off, driven through the cover region for one.
Well done, Stoneman! Curran strays on the pads but gets away. He bowls it full on the pads, Khawaja clips it away. Stoneman at mid-wicket dives to his right and manages to save 3  runs for his side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full outside off, left alone by UK.

Overpitched outside off, Khawaja mistimes the cover drive. He manages to get it in the gap and gets a couple for that. Clarke, on air, observes that his head position isn't the best there as it is seen falling over. Quickly goes on to add that it would get better with time in the middle.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. Back-to-back maidens for Ali.
This flighted ball is driven back to where he came from.
Flatter on off, slapped towards cover-point for nothing.
Warner goes back to this one and punches it towards covers. 'Nice bowling, Mo,' shouts Jonny from behind.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Floated full outside off, driven towards covers.
Fuller on off, driven towards wide mid off, where Broad does well with a tumble. A run results though.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Warner gets ahead in defense to this delivery.

Michael Clarke was considered to be a good player of spin and he makes this valid point on air. We saw Khawaja use his feet to come down the track twice in the previous over. On the first instance, he went away from the line of the ball before having to adjust to get close to the ball. In the second time though, he came down in a straight line and defended the ball right under his eye line. Clarke feels that the second instance is the right way to do it as the ball is covered well by the batter. In making room by coming down, chances are that the ball might spin past the edge.
Hurled outside off, Warner leaves it unharmed.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
A touch short on the body, pulled away through mid-wicket for a couple.

Double change. Tom Curran to have a bowl now. Often we have seen in the sport that performance with one aspect rubs off on the player who ends up doing well in another aspect as well. Curran had a good outing with the bat today and should carry his confidence to his performance with the ball.
Khawaja comes down the track and dead-bats this one. Maiden to begin for Mo.
Loopy ball around off, forward defense on display.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Ahh! Khawaja perhaps makes his intentions to come down the track clear. Ali fires this just outside off. Usman had to adjust to get forward and block.
Floated around off, defended off the front foot.
Flatter outside off, cut towards point.
Surprise change! Moeen Ali is the first change bowler for England. Root's decision to go to his out-of-form off spinner might have something to do with the presence of two left-handers at the crease.
Broad straightens his line and bowls it on middle and leg. Warner clips it through square leg. Warner wanted two immediately and Khawaja responded well.
Length ball outside off, Warner covers his stumps and lets it be.
Bowled in line of the off stump, Warner gets behind that in defense.

Interesting point. Both the sides have been having similar problems with their top order. For the hosts, Bancroft and Khawaja haven't really fired in the series, just like England's top order. But Australia haven't really been two or three down for nothing. They have somehow managed to hold fort and let the runs mount.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Hip high length ball on the pads tucked away through backward square leg for one.
Full in length around off and middle, defended right back towards the bowler.
Warner drives this one through the cover region and picks up a couple.
Fuller in length, pushed towards covers.
Another delivery on a length on off, defended towards mid off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Length ball on the stumps, defended from the crease.
Landed in line of the off stump, Warner goes back and offers a straight bat face in defense.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Hurled outside off, left alone.
Jonny Bairstow is wearing a black arm band. The reason for that is that it is the 20th death anniversary of his father, who committed suicide.

Similar delivery, Warner looks to tuck it away but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball rolls towards backward square leg as David takes off for a single. Bairstow rushes there and fires a wild throw at the bowler's end but Warner is well in anyway.

FOUR! Not a bad ball but still put away. Broad lands it on a length in line of the leg stump, Warner hops a touch and plays the flick. The ball takes the inner edge and goes off the thigh pads towards the fine leg fence. It has enough legs on it to roll away to the fence, in spite of Bairstow chasing it down.
Full on off, driven towards mid off.
Broad comes from over the wicket and hurls it on a length in line of the stumps. Warner stands tall and blocks that.
Length ball in line of the stumps, Khawaja gets it off the inner half towards mid-wicket for nothing.
Full pitched ball on off, pushed down the ground, to be intercepted by the man at mid off.
Full and outside off, Khawaja just lets it be.
Much better from Jimmy. Just shortens his length a touch and angles it across Khawaja. The southpaw has a poke at that only for the ball to whiz past the outer edge through to the keeper.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Nicely played. Anderson serves this a touch fuller than a good length, Khawaja punches it down the ground past mid off. Gets two for the shot.
Warner drives this one towards mid off.
Outside off, left alone.

It is seen that England seem to be learning from their mistakes. They have been bowling on the shorter side in the series generally. But in this innings so far, Anderson and Broad have been bowling on the good length and fuller length areas and have made the batsmen play. Ian Healy thinks it to be a better tactic as that increases the chances of a wicket, like it did with Bancroft's dismissal.
Fuller in length, driven through covers to rotate strike.
Warner has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Driven through mid on by the batsman.
Broad bowls it outside off from round the wicket, David lets it alone.
This is outside off, left alone.
On the pads, flicked to mid-wicket.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Length ball outside off, guided towards gully.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Anderson runs in and bowls it full on off and middle. Usman drives it back towards the bowler.
Outside off, driven nicely through covers for a couple.
Warner hangs back to this one and blocks this.
Khawaja gets going with a flick through mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller on off, defended back towards the bowler.
Usman Khawaja is the next man in. It would be safe to assume that he is battling to save his place in the side as he hasn't got the scores expected from him.

OUT! Broad strikes straightaway and gets his 399th Test wicket in style. He runs in from over the wicket to Bancroft and hurls it on a fuller length around off. The opener looks to drive this down the ground but gets beaten on the inside due to the nip back on that. The ball goes through the gate and disturbs the pink-coloured woodwork behind. He has to walk back for a duck and England are up and running. On further looks, Bancroft's bat seems to come down in the direction of mid off, thereby leaving a huge gap between bat and pad. He has been dismissed in this series off deliveries from a similar length and that should get him thinking.

The on-air commentators analyse Warner's run taking method. They opine that as the southpaw has this knack of hitting the cricket ball powerfully, the fielders in a single-saving position often tend to stand a touch deeper. This helps Warner exploit that to tap and run, which he did even today.
Broad runs in from round the wicket and lands it on a length on off. Warner pats it in front of covers and gets to the other end to open his account.
Stuart Broad to share the new ball from the other end.
Maiden over to begin for Anderson. He lands it on the stumps, Bancroft blocks it nicely.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Fuller in line of the stumps, flicked to the man at mid-wicket.
Bowled on a length outside off, left alone by Cameron.
Angling in to the batter, Bancroft keeps it out towards mid-wicket.
Anderson steams in from over the wicket and lands it on a length outside off. Bancroft covers the stumps and lets that go.
